review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–106). It declares a single theorem, `local_automorphism_ODE_group_law_of_contDiffAt`. Its conclusion is an existential statement (`∃ ε > 0, ε<δ ∧ ∀ s t, |s|<ε → |t|<ε → g (s+t)=g s*g t`) with many analytic hypotheses, so it could never be a simp lemma. The file has no `@[simp]` attributes, no `simp` sets and no definitions that would need unfolding lemmas, so it has no simp interface of its own to review. Inside the proof, `simpa only` is used twice: once with `id_eq`, and once with `Function.comp_def, one_smul` for the derivative of the shifted function. Everything else is explicit `rw` using `zero_add`, `hg0`, `ambientAut_apply`, `one_apply` and `mul_apply`. `one_apply` and `mul_apply` are already `@[simp]` in TendstoAmbientLocallyUniformly.lean (lines 52–55), and these rewrites run cleanly here. One observation outside this file: many sibling files use the same pattern of rewriting `ambientAut_apply` and then `one_apply`/`mul_apply` (for example SmallAutomorphismsHaveNonzero.lean line 59, ProjectedChartLeftDifferential.lean lines 73 and 96, and ProductCurveLocalFlow.lean line 90). That pattern hints that `ambientAut_one`/`ambientAut_mul`-style lemmas might be useful. If added, those lemmas would belong where `ambientAut` is defined (in LocalAutomorphismODEGroup or an upstream file), not in this target file, so I did not report it as a finding here.
